label: Product-dependent adoption and adoption-dependent product in every actual supply route
definition: OutputFounded m I adoption product says that neither of the two selected role-events has independently supplied contribution I, every admitted and actually exercised record with adoption as effect requires product among all its joint contributors, and every such record with product as effect requires adoption among its contributors. Other contributors, including the source's own necessary activity, may also be present. It describes two-sided productive prerequisites over all represented actual alternatives. It does not describe mere reference to, truth about, or semantic individuation by an output.
note: A task-local application of the existing Supply/Trap standard, not a new definition of adequacy, agency or metaphysical grounding. The source AND product record illustrates why an additional conjunct is not an independent alternative. An exercised source-only record to adoption defeats the adoption-needs-product clause; an exercised source-only record directly to product defeats the product-needs-adoption clause while preserving output-dependent adoption. Mere admission defeats neither actual prerequisite. The interpretation requires warranted contributor classification, actual exercise, all-route scope and applicability of inductive supply. A semantic or constitutive dependence on the effect cannot be imported into this productive relation without an additional argument. Direct personal and impersonal exercise are tested equally. No claim that all actual causal or grounding explanation has this structure is made. See docs/notes/psr-self-application-756.md#actual-productive-exercise-and-the-output-dependence-test-2026-11-24.
